# attestation-issuer

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from servlets/attestation-issuer/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/attestation-issuer.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `attestation-issuer` component of `servlets/attestation-issuer`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.servlet.attestation`: generated from its catalogue, [attestation-issuer.json](../../servlets/attestation-issuer/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/attestation-issuer.json), by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_ATTESTER_`, `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_`, `OIDF_WALLET_`, `OIDF_ENTRA_`, `OIDF_CIMD_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_ISSUER` ([components](../development/settings-catalogue.md#components)).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `challengeRequired` (init-param) | `false` | Whether an instance-key proof must carry a challenge from /federation/attestation/challenge; the issuance servlet enforces it and the two discovery servlets advertise it, each from its own init-param, so set the three alike | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false, in any case: the servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and its path answers 503 (under development yes, no, 1, 0, on and off are read as false, with a warning naming the strict spelling); before 0.6.0 anything but true meant false. Servlets that disagree advertise one thing and enforce another | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_REQUIRED` (init-param `customClaimsRequired`, then system property `oidf.attestation.custom.claims.required`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_REQUIRED`) | Unset; a list | Claims every instance-key proof must carry besides the protocol's, comma-separated: enforced by the issuance servlet and advertised as custom_claims_required; the init-param customClaimsRequired on each of those two servlets wins over the system property and the environment | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Split at commas and spaces from 0.6.0 (at commas only before); a claim a client does not send refuses its every issuance | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_SUPPORTED` (init-param `customClaimsSupported`, then system property `oidf.attestation.custom.claims.supported`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTATION_CUSTOM_CLAIMS_SUPPORTED`) | Unset; a list | Claims the client attestation service document advertises as custom_claims_supported, comma-separated; advertised only; the init-param customClaimsSupported on the metadata servlet wins over the system property and the environment | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the metadata servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Split at commas and spaces from 0.6.0 (at commas only before); nothing enforces it | Any | No |
| `challengeEndpointEnabled` (init-param) | `true` | Whether the client attestation service document advertises challenge_endpoint; on the metadata servlet | **Doesn't start**: Set to anything but true or false, in any case: the metadata servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (under development yes, no, 1, 0, on and off are read as false, with a warning naming the strict spelling); before 0.6.0 anything but true meant false | Any | No |
| `attestationSigningAlgValuesSupported` (init-param) | `RS256,PS256,ES256`; a list | The algorithms the client attestation service document advertises as attestation_signing_alg_values_supported, comma-separated; on the metadata servlet, advertised only | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,': the metadata servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (before 0.6.0 it meant the default). Split at commas and spaces; nothing checks it against the keys attestations are signed with | Any | No |
| `openBaoUrl` (init-param) | Unset | OpenBao's address for attestation signing keys (a client's attestation_signing_key_ref), on the issuance servlet; used only with openBaoToken, and with either unset both come from OIDF_OPENBAO_URL and OIDF_OPENBAO_TOKEN and their fallbacks (hosted-entity-signing) | **Per request**: Wrong or unreachable: a client whose attestation_signing_key_ref needs the vault is refused with server_error | Any | Yes |
| `openBaoToken` (init-param) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The OpenBao token for the same, on the issuance servlet; used only with openBaoUrl | **Per request**: Refused by OpenBao: as for openBaoUrl | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_FEDERATION_ENTITY` (system property `oidf.attester.federation.entity`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_FEDERATION_ENTITY`) | Unset; an http or https URL | An OpenID Federation entity whose signed statement maps SPIFFE IDs to clients, consulted before the CIMD document and PingFederate's client store, and trusted only through a chain to a pinned trust anchor (OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_ANCHOR_JWKS); an entity the anchor stops vouching for loses its clients within 300 s | **First request**: Named with no trust anchor pinned: the attester refuses to build its client sources at its first request | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK` (system property `oidf.attester.signing.jwk`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_JWK`) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The attester's private signing key as an inline JWK, applied to every client the federation entity or the CIMD document describes; never read from those documents | **Per request**: Missing or malformed: those clients are refused (invalid_client) at issuance, unless an entry names a signing_key_ref | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_CIMD_URL` (system property `oidf.attester.cimd.url`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_CIMD_URL`) | Unset; an http or https URL | A Client ID Metadata Document as a client source, honoured only with OIDF_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=development (plan item M-1, F-0067): the document hands the attester every client's bindings and trust roots, so whoever answers at the URL chooses the keys the attester accepts | **First request**: Set outside development: at the attester's first request the cimd source is left out with an ERROR naming the variable, and the other sources keep serving | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `OIDF_CIMD_TRUST_BUNDLES` (system property `oidf.cimd.trust.bundles`, then env `OIDF_CIMD_TRUST_BUNDLES`) | Unset | Only whether it is set counts: set, with OIDF_DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE=development, the client attestation service document lists cimd in client_metadata_sources_supported; nothing reads its value or enforces it | **Not checked**: Its value is never read | Any | No |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_OP_ISSUER` (system property `oidf.attester.op.issuer`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_OP_ISSUER`) | Unset | The hosted attester's own entity id, the relying party in a wallet provider's trust chain; with a trust controller configured (OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_CONTROLLER_HOST) it turns on federation-backed wallet provider trust, in preference to OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS | **Per request**: Wrong: no wallet provider's chain resolves, and every wallet instance attestation is refused. Read at deploy as well as at the first request, like the attester's other settings | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS` (system property `oidf.wallet.provider.jwks`, then env `OIDF_WALLET_PROVIDER_JWKS`) | Unset; a JSON object | Wallet providers trusted statically, a JSON object of provider entity id to its JWK Set, used only when federation-backed wallet trust is not configured; the keys are trusted with no trust chain | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object: the issuance and metadata servlets' parts are FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (before 0.6.0 it was ignored without a word, and every wallet instance attestation refused); an entry that is not a JWK Set is skipped | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ENTRA_AGENT_DIRECTORY` (system property `oidf.entra.agent.directory`, then env `OIDF_ENTRA_AGENT_DIRECTORY`) | Unset; a JSON object | The Entra Agent ID directory, a JSON object of asserted oid to directory entry, which registers the entra-directory asserted-context resolver; its ceiling only narrows an evidenced one | **Doesn't start**: Not a JSON object: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting (before 0.6.0 no resolver was registered, without a word) | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_ENTRIES_URL` (system property `oidf.attester.spire.entries.url`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_SPIRE_ENTRIES_URL`) | Unset; an http or https URL | A SPIRE entries endpoint whose selectors are added to an instance's workload attributes at issuance; unset, no introspection | **Doesn't start**: Not an http or https URL: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting. Unreachable: the instance gets no selectors | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_ISSUED_TTL` (system property `oidf.attester.max.issued.ttl`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_ISSUED_TTL`) | `3600`; seconds, 60 to 64800 | The longest lifetime, in seconds, the attester gives an attestation it issues: a client's attestation_issued_ttl above it is refused in production and clamped to it with a warning in development. 64800 (18 hours, the AI Agent Profile's ceiling) is the most it may be | **First request**: Not a whole number, or outside 60 to 64800: issuance answers 500 server_error naming the variable, from the first request, in either profile | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (system property `oidf.attester.max.body.bytes`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_BODY_BYTES`) | `32768`; a whole number, 4096 to 262144 | The largest request body POST /federation/attestation reads, in bytes (32 KiB by default, 4-256 KiB); a body declared or found larger is answered 413 invalid_request with no more of it read | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 4096 to 262144: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_ISSUANCE_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE` (system property `oidf.attester.issuance.requests.per.minute`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_ISSUANCE_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`) | `60`; a whole number, 1 to 100000 | How many issuance requests one client address may make in a minute before POST /federation/attestation answers 429 temporarily_unavailable with Retry-After; counted in Redis (oidf:cas:limit:issue) when OIDF_REDIS_URL is set, else by each node for itself. The client address is the remote address, or behind a proxy OIDF_TRUSTED_PROXIES lists, the forwarding hop it does not list | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1 to 100000: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503. Behind a proxy that is not listed, every caller shares the proxy's allowance | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_CLIENT_INDEX_REFRESH_SECONDS` (system property `oidf.attester.client.index.refresh.seconds`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_CLIENT_INDEX_REFRESH_SECONDS`) | `30`; seconds, 5 to 3600 | How often, in seconds, the attester rebuilds its index of PingFederate's attestation clients (every client read once, on a background thread); evidence no indexed client accepts rebuilds it at once, at most once every 5 s. A client added, changed, disabled or deleted in PingFederate is seen at issuance within this time while PingFederate's clients can be read; while they cannot, the index is served for at most four of these intervals, then issuance answers 503 | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 5 to 3600: the issuance servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and the endpoint answers 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_ATTESTER_CORS_ORIGINS` (system property `oidf.attester.cors.origins`, then env `OIDF_ATTESTER_CORS_ORIGINS`) | Unset; a list | The browser origins, such as https://console.example, allowed to read the attester configuration documents (/.well-known/client-attester and /federation/attester-configuration) with GET, space- or comma-separated; unset, no origin is, since workloads and SDKs fetch them from servers. An origin listed gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin naming it and Vary: Origin | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, such as ', ,', or an entry that is not scheme://host[:port] with no path: the configuration servlet's part is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and its documents answer 503. An origin left out is refused by the browser, not by the server | Any | Yes |
